title: Turning Left From a One-Way Street: Always Start From the Far-LEFT Curb Lane (Never From the Right/Middle Lane!)

no_head_on_same_lane.note: No two vehicles face each other head-on within the same lane; northbound blue sedan at bottom and southbound cars at top are in separate approaches.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No car interior or steering wheel is visible; all vehicles seen only from exterior bird's-eye view.

single_bulb_signal.note: Overhead signal in center shows single green lens lit, other lenses dark.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Bottom vertical approach shows blue sedan heading north but positioned in the west/left lane, with yellow center implied to its right, and top approach shows four lanes all heading south straddling a yellow center line - driving on the left side, not the right.

zero_text.note: All signs, plates and storefronts appear as blank colored shapes with no legible letters or numbers.

scene_match.note: Blue sedan at bottom does show a left-turn arrow from far-left position onto cross street, but vertical street is depicted as two-way with opposing traffic top vs bottom, not a 3-lane one-way origin.

result.summary: Fails right-hand traffic geometry with blue car on wrong side and lacks one-way depiction, teaching wrong-way positioning as correct.

teaching_correct.note: On a two-way street as drawn, starting a left turn from the far-left/wrong-side lane teaches wrong-way driving; cyclist riding on double-yellow center also models illegal position.

result.what_i_see: Bird's-eye view of an urban intersection with a blue sedan at the bottom in the left lane following a light-blue left-turn arrow onto an east-west street with double-yellow center where a cyclist and gray sedan travel.
